Treatments/Implantology

Single & Multi-Tooth Dental Implants

Biocompatible titanium fixtures surgically placed into the jawbone to permanently replace missing tooth roots.

Indicative Duration: [TBD:service_durations]•Indicative Fee: [TBD:service_prices]

Procedure Overview

Dental implants represent the gold standard in tooth replacement. Composed of medical-grade titanium or zirconia, the fixture integrates naturally with jawbone tissue through osseointegration, providing a solid foundation for a bespoke ceramic crown.

Clinical Indications

This procedure is typically indicated for patients exhibiting the following clinical presentations:

  • •Single or multiple missing teeth
  • •Difficulty chewing or speaking due to tooth loss
  • •Prevention of bone resorption in edentulous areas
  • •Alternative to removable dentures or bridge preparation of healthy adjacent teeth

Step-by-Step Clinical Protocol

1

CBCT 3D bone scan evaluation and digital treatment planning

2

Minimally invasive surgical placement of implant fixture

3

Healing period (osseointegration) of 8 to 16 weeks

4

Abutment connection and precision digital scan

5

Delivery and screw-retained or cement-retained porcelain crown

Pre-Appointment Care

  • Complete medical review including HbA1c (diabetic check) and blood pressure.
  • Discontinue smoking as it significantly impairs osseointegration.

Post-Procedure Care

  • Maintain soft diet for the initial 48 hours.
  • Apply cold compression externally to minimize mild postoperative swelling.

Treatment FAQs

What is the success rate of dental implants?

In healthy candidates with adequate bone volume and good oral hygiene, dental implants have an internationally documented success rate of 95% to 98%.
